Reuters — first published 23 Sep 2026 23:51 BST; UPDATED 24 Sep 2026 12:44 BST (Kyiv)

HEADLINE: Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine, damage maternity clinic

Russian drone and missile strikes on Ukraine's capital Kyiv and its northeast killed eight people on Thursday in attacks that included a maternity hospital and a farm, officials said.

- Two people died in the latest assault on Kyiv, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who was in New York for the UN General Assembly.
- A separate Russian attack on a vegetable storage facility at a farm in a village of the northeastern Kharkiv region killed six people and injured a further 12, prosecutors said.
- The overnight barrage around Ukraine included an unspecified number of hypersonic and ballistic missiles, 282 drones and other weapons, Ukraine's air force said.
- In Kyiv, eight people were injured as well as the two fatalities, one of whom was in the parking lot of the maternity hospital, city mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Part of the hospital's facade, windows and doors were damaged; no patients or medics were injured.
- Police said nine homes, a post office, warehouses and dozens of cars were also damaged in Kyiv.
- Authorities in the northwestern region of Rivne said infrastructure was damaged in overnight strikes that continued into Thursday morning. Volyn region bordering Poland also came under attack.
- In the Black Sea port of Odesa, military administration head Serhiy Lysak said overnight Russian strikes damaged a medical facility and shattered windows in nearby houses and a school.
- Moldova's President Maia Sandu said four Russian drones crossed into its airspace and at least one exploded; Romania said a drone also crashed in its territory. NATO member Poland said it deployed aviation twice on Thursday due to Russian attacks on Ukraine.
- Russia's defence ministry said its forces hit Ukrainian defence facilities, logistics and telecoms centres, as well as vessels used by the military. (Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-strikes-hit-ukrainian-military-linked-facilities-vessels-2026-09-24/)

QUOTE (Zelenskiy, on Telegram): "As people were sleeping, flashes from explosions lit up the sky. Once again, the main targets of their strike were Kyiv and civilian infrastructure, residential buildings, a maternity hospital, energy infrastructure, and logistics."
QUOTE (Zelenskiy): "Right now, the United States has the opportunity to respond strongly. We need ballistic interceptors to protect lives."

Moscow has stepped up its air war in recent months, deploying more of its faster and harder-to-stop drones while Ukraine is short of interceptors to down ballistic missiles.
